display.purpose: Home promise and the largest public-facing statements.

headline.purpose: Page-level task headings and dark-surface introductions.

body.purpose: Instructions, controls, record content, and recovery copy.

label.purpose: Table headers, workspace labels, and compact metadata.

shadows.name: featured-record
shadows.purpose: Ambient lift for the signature case-journey sheet only.

shadows.name: toast
shadows.purpose: Short-lived system feedback above the ledger.

motion.name: view-entry
motion.purpose: A 10px upward settle with a brief fade and blur when changing views.

motion.name: ledger-draw
motion.purpose: Draws case-history rules from the top to explain sequence.

motion.name: control-state
motion.purpose: Fast hover and focus response for fields, rows, and cards.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Effectively removes all animation and transition when reduced motion is requested.

narrative.overview:
JanSeva behaves like a clear, well-kept public record rather than a generic software dashboard. A deep ink service rail anchors broad sheets of cool civic paper; ruled divisions, tabular references, and an authored case-history line make state feel durable and inspectable. The tone is calm, respectful, and precise without borrowing the ceremonial language of an official institution.

The system puts action before chrome. Service teal is concentrated on the strongest next step, while brass marks attention and current state. Large EB Garamond statements provide civic gravity; Lato keeps controls, records, and recovery copy plain. Density stays moderate, whitespace remains generous, and motion explains arrival or state rather than decorating it.
keyCharacteristics: Deep ink navigation against cool, lightly ruled paper.
Unequal raise and track actions that make the primary task unmistakable.
Ledger-like references, tables, timelines, and status markers.
Selective lift reserved for the featured record, transient feedback, and modals.
Self-hosted EB Garamond and Lato, with tabular numerals for references and counts.
Restrained, directional motion with a complete reduced-motion path.

rules.name: The Scarce Teal Rule
rules.body: Service teal identifies an action or a meaningful current state; it is not a decorative wash.

rules.name: The Brass Means Attention Rule
rules.body: Brass marks selection, progression, or a deliberate civic cue. Never use it as a second primary action color.

rules.name: The Paper, Not White Rule
rules.body: The application ground remains cool paper, while near-white is reserved for raised or bounded ledger surfaces.

rules.name: The Authority and Utility Rule
rules.body: EB Garamond speaks for promises and record headings; Lato operates the service.

rules.name: The Reference Is Data Rule
rules.body: Case IDs, dates, and counts use tabular numerals and remain visually distinct from prose.

rules.name: The Ledger Is Flat Rule
rules.body: Ordinary panels, forms, tables, and service cards use a rule and a paper shift, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Lift Has Meaning Rule
rules.body: Elevation signals a featured record, transient feedback, or a blocking layer; it never exists solely to make a surface look premium.

dos: Do lead every surface with the resident's next action and a plain explanation of what follows.
Do use broad rules, aligned rows, and tabular references to make case history feel durable and inspectable.
Do preserve the unequal visual weight of raise and track actions.
Do keep prototype disclosure visible wherever the service could be mistaken for an official channel.
Do pair every status color with a readable label, and preserve 44px minimum touch targets and visible focus.
Do keep entry and ledger-line motion restrained, directional, and fully removable through reduced motion.
donts: Don't turn the interface into an equal-card dashboard or add decorative metric tiles to fill space.
Don't use gradients, glass effects, ornamental government motifs, or institutional seals.
Don't spread teal across passive surfaces or use brass as a competing call-to-action color.
Don't add shadows to ordinary panels, fields, tables, or service cards.
Don't replace the serif-and-sans hierarchy with a single generic UI face.
Don't hide recovery, status, privacy, or prototype limits behind color, hover, or secondary navigation.
